card.name: Risk-benefit phrases in NSAID warnings
card.fires_on: The word "of" or "risk" in "benefits are expected to outweigh the risk of recurrent CV thrombotic events" in NSAID label warnings. It also fires on a few other warning words, such as "affect" and "events".

modes.label: Outweigh the risk of
modes.description: The word "of" (or "risk") closing the phrase "benefits are expected to outweigh the risk" in label warnings.
modes.example: Avoid the use of celecoxib in patients with a recent MI unless the benefits are expected to outweigh the risk<< of>> recurrent CV thrombotic events.

modes.label: Other warning wording
modes.description: Scattered words in warnings about infection or cardiovascular events, such as "affect" or "events".
modes.example: Since TNF mediates inflammation and modulates cellular immune responses, the possibility exists for TNF blockers, including CIMZIA, to<< affect>> host defenses against infections and malignancies.

card.plain: It lights up on the stock label wording that weighs benefit against risk, mostly in NSAID heart-risk warnings.
